value.rationale: Ayyer–Podder solve the stationary measure but leave spatial ordering uncharacterized for m=3. The newly calculated unique q_c(p) distinguishes genuine finite-wavevector damped oscillations from eventually positive correlations, gives an r-times-exponential boundary law and a diverging oscillation wavelength with exponent 1/2. The minimality contrast with m=2 is structural: two-neighbour transfer roots are always real, whereas m=3 supports nonreal modes. These are physically motivated, parameter-global and not an arbitrary finite-size slice. No thermodynamic phase transition or application beyond stationary spatial statistics is claimed.
